summary.headline: Library trustees approved repairing damaged concrete under the book drop and agreed to draft a letter clarifying DPW grounds maintenance responsibilities.
summary.summary: The Library Board of Trustees reviewed proposed Community Preservation Act signage for the building facade restoration with a Community Preservation Committee representative. The trustees authorized the director to coordinate concrete repairs under the exterior book drop using State Aid funds and voted to draft a formal letter to town leadership seeking clear maintenance responsibilities between the library and the Department of Public Works. The board also reviewed the library director's annual performance evaluation and established five professional goals for the coming year.

topics.title: Community Preservation Act recognition signage
topics.summary: A representative from the Community Preservation Committee met with the trustees to discuss wording and formatting for recognition plaques on past library projects. The board agreed to simplified wording attributing the historic restoration of the library facade to Southborough residents through the Community Preservation Act.
key_details: Signage will recognize CPA funding for the facade restoration and the Southborough history room.
The board agreed to remove the phrase 'and preservation' to make the wording more concise.
Exterior signage is expected to cost approximately $400 to $500, with interior signage costing less.
The library director will seek formal quotes from Crown Trophy once CPC confirms approval of the text on May 21.
topics.outcome: Consensus reached on plaque wording; CPC will review on May 21 and quotes will be obtained.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board reviewed and approved the meeting minutes from April 13 with minor typographical and clarifying revisions.
key_details: Corrections were made regarding parking lot pothole repairs and phrasing of trustee evaluation submissions.

topics.title: Director's report and facility updates
topics.summary: The library director provided updates on staff activities, programs, and operational technology. Verizon is discontinuing hardwired copper phone lines, prompting the library to transition its public fax service to an internet-based machine through Fax24.
key_details: Security camera installation project is finished and will be paid through State Aid funds.
QPR suicide prevention training for staff is scheduled for June 1 in partnership with Youth and Family Services.
The annual library book sale is scheduled for June 6, with donations accepted up to three boxes or 50 books per visit.
The public fax machine was used three times in the past month and remains an active service for residents.
topics.outcome: Information received; director to proceed with the internet-based fax machine upgrade.

topics.title: Book drop concrete replacement and grounds maintenance
topics.summary: The board discussed damaged concrete beneath the library book drop that creates a tripping hazard and drainage concern. Following confusion over whether the Department of Public Works or the library is responsible for exterior grounds repairs, the board voted to fund the concrete replacement using library State Aid funds and to draft a joint letter to town officials requesting clear jurisdictional boundaries.
key_details: The concrete platform under the book drop has failed patchwork and requires complete removal and repouring.
Facilities Director John Parent inspected the site and identified a vendor who can perform the work for under $5,000.
Trustees expressed frustration that grounds maintenance tasks such as lawn care, parking lot repairs, and tree trimming have increasingly been refused by DPW.
Trustees voted to have two members collaborate with the director on a letter to the DPW, Facilities Department, Town Administrator, and Select Board.
topics.outcome: Approved proceeding with the concrete repair under $5,000 using State Aid, and voted to draft a letter clarifying DPW and library grounds maintenance responsibilities.
topics.why_it_matters: Clarifying maintenance jurisdiction directly affects how municipal funds and library aid are spent on property upkeep, safety, and infrastructure repairs.

topics.title: FY24 expense and budget review
topics.summary: The director reviewed remaining FY24 operating budget lines as the fiscal year nears completion. A recent $1,190 landscaping bill was absorbed within the regular dues budget line rather than drawing from State Aid.
key_details: Curtis Landscaping bill of $1,190 was paid from available funds in the dues line.
Salary projections show adequate remaining funds to finish the fiscal year.
Monthly digital borrowing expenses through Hoopla exceeded $1,000.70 due to high resident usage.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; expenses will continue to be drawn down through the close of the fiscal year.

topics.title: Director evaluation process and FY25 goals
topics.summary: The chair reported on legal guidance regarding Open Meeting Law compliance for the director's annual performance evaluation, noting that trustee feedback must be discussed openly rather than compiled privately. The trustees reviewed the director's performance over the past year and adopted five focal goals for the upcoming year.
key_details: Marguerite Landry noted case law cited by the Assistant Town Administrator prohibiting offline collation of board evaluations.
Trustees commended the director for website migration, marketing consistency, staff mentorship, and community programming.

Five goals were set: supporting community partner roles, documenting space reconfiguration procedures, maximizing time and facility resources, attending a national library conference, and researching library storage and space improvements.
Under the non-union Salary Administration Plan schedule, the director is eligible for a 5 percent increase (comprising a 2.5 percent merit step and a 2.5 percent cost of living adjustment).
topics.outcome: Agreed on performance evaluation letter additions and finalized five director goals.

topics.title: Juneteenth holiday schedule adjustment
topics.summary: The director informed trustees of building closure requirements surrounding the Juneteenth holiday. Because full-time staff schedules are split across Fridays and Saturdays, the library will be closed on both Friday, June 19, and Saturday, June 20.
key_details: Juneteenth is an official town holiday on Friday, June 19.
The library must also close Saturday, June 20, to afford equitable holiday time to staff scheduled on Saturdays.
topics.outcome: Information noted; holiday closures will be finalized at the June meeting.

votes.motion: To approve proceeding with the concrete repair under the book drop in coordination with the Facilities Department, funded through State Aid.

To appoint trustees Janet Maney and Jane Davis to draft a letter concerning the chain of responsibility for library grounds maintenance addressed to the DPW, Town Administrator, Facilities, and Select Board.
